transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I'm here because... things at work have been really intense lately. I'm a buyer, and I just can't shake this feeling that people at the office, and even some of our vendors, are tracking my buys. Which is wild because vendors are supposed to be professional, right? Like this one guy we deal with, he sells us these imported ceramic mugs, and he always wears these incredibly flashy ties. Last week it was bright yellow with little golf clubs on it. I don't even know who plays golf anymore, honestly. My uncle used to play golf all the time, but he messed up his shoulder slipping on some ice a few years ago. It was a whole ordeal, he had to get surgery and everything, and his physical therapist was just awful to him. 

But... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the vendors. Yeah, they're tracking me and messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. My supervisor keeps pulling up the reports and showing me that the data doesn't prove that they're doing it, but I just know they are. It's really getting to me, so... yeah, that's what really made me come in.
About how long have you been feeling that people at work and the vendors are tracking you?

Well, it's been going on for a while. I'd say roughly ten months now. Ten months of just... knowing they're watching me. And the voice, too, that started around the same time. It's been ten months of that. Which is funny, because ten months ago was right around the time I bought my new car. It's a Honda Civic, silver. I really wanted the blue one, but the dealership didn't have it in stock, and the salesman was incredibly pushy. He kept trying to upsell me on this undercoating package that I know is just a scam. My dad always told me never to buy the undercoating. He was a mechanic for thirty years, worked at this little shop downtown that used to be a gas station in the fifties. They still had the old pumps out front, just for show, you know? Anyway, the salesman was wearing this terrible cologne, smelled like pine needles and cheap aftershave... but yeah, about ten months.
During these past ten months, have you had times where you felt unusually energized, high, or wired, needing much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, definitely. I get these stretches where I feel just... electric. Like the whole city is opening up for me, you know? Like I can do anything. Actually, speaking of the city, they just started tearing up the pavement on 5th Avenue right by my apartment, and it's a total mess. The jackhammers start at like 6 AM. The guys running them always wear those neon green vests, which reminds me of this crossing guard we had in elementary school. Mr. Henderson. He used to give out butterscotch candies, but only if you looked both ways twice. I don't even like butterscotch, it's too sweet, it always gets stuck in your teeth... but anyway, what were we talking about? 

Right, being wired. Yeah, I get super energized like that. But then the problem is, if someone at the office questions a purchase order I made, or if my supervisor tells me to slow down, I just explode. I snap way harder than I mean to. Like, I yelled at our shipping guy the other day just for using the clear packing tape instead of the brown paper kind. Which really does mess up the recycling process, but still, I probably shouldn't have yelled.
Do you still hear the voice or feel like you're being tracked during times when you aren't feeling energized or wired?

Yeah, definitely. Even when I have those calmer stretches... like, there was a time recently where I was actually sleeping normally again, not feeling like I was running the whole market or totally wired. But I still spent a few weeks fully believing people were tracking my buys. And I was still hearing that voice when I was back in the stockroom. Which is super annoying because the stockroom is where we keep all the overflow for the seasonal stuff. Right now it's just packed with these cheap plastic Halloween decorations. They smell awful, like that weird factory chemical smell? It reminds me of this factory tour I went on in high school. We went to a place that made rubber boots. The smell was so strong I actually got a headache, and the bus ride back was terrible because the suspension on the school bus was completely shot. Every pothole felt like we were crashing. My friend Tyler was sitting next to me, and he had brought this giant bag of salt and vinegar chips, which just made my stomach turn even more... 

But wait, what was the question? Oh, right, the voice and the tracking. Yeah, even when I'm not feeling all electric and I'm sleeping fine, that stuff doesn't go away. It was still happening for a few weeks during that calm period.
